source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 5 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 358,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 36 MW supports roughly 900 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation average, the same power supports roughly 3,600 racks. The arithmetic is an illustration of the range, not an operator claim. Power density per square foot is low at either assumption, which suggests the floor plan is sized for mixed colocation workloads rather than purpose-built GPU clusters, though the operator has not published a breakdown.

The certification stack qualifies this campus for a wide range of regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 cover financial and operational controls audits. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for controlled defense-related technical data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal information system security controls. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the attestation standard underlying the SOC reports. Which tenants occupy the campus is not published.

Among Oregon facilities this site has read, Hillsboro 5 ranks first by published IT capacity, accounting for 36 of the 182 MW published across the six Oregon facilities that have reported a figure at all. Oregon has 133 facilities mapped in OpenStreetMap, and only six have published a megawatt figure, so the 182 MW total understates actual state capacity by an unknown amount. Oregon's grid context relative to AI demand is not published on the operator's spec page and is therefore not assessed here.
